title: monotonic-ingest-sequencer-delayed-charge-protocol-for-duplicate-suppression
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Customers sometimes get double-billed when client retries or network retries cause the same logical request to be ingested more than once by our front-end fleet. Incidents and postmortems show two common classes of failure: (1) short-window duplicate submissions due to at-least-once client behaviour and transient network retries, and (2) delayed duplicate replays from intermediate proxies or SDK retries after failover.

Goal:
Design and ship a server-side protocol that prevents duplicate usage charges for common retry patterns while preserving low-latency charging for normal requests and keeping quota enforcement accurate. Must be compatible with existing clients (no immediate SDK upgrade required) and support an opt-in stronger mode for upgraded clients.

Scope:
- Implement a per-customer monotonic ingest sequencer and provisional-charge + commit protocol in the ingest tier.
- Add server-side dedupe window and probabilistic admission path for stateless clients.
- Expose client-facing guidance and SDK helper to generate monotonic sequence tokens.
- Add reconciliation tooling to sweep provisional entries and finalize/cancel charges.
- Do NOT change token accounting semantics in downstream billing pipeline for this rollout; use a reconciliation step to emit final billable events.

Out of scope:
- Complete rework of downstream billing pipeline.
- Long-tail reconciliation for historic data beyond 90 days (handled by separate finance playbook).
design_notes:
High-level protocol:
1) Client monotonic sequence (client_seq): upgraded SDKs attach a client_seq and client_epoch per-customer API key. client_seq is strictly increasing for each logical request. For single-process clients, this is monotonic counter; for multi-process clients, SDKs provide a small vector-clock helper.
2) Ingest node actions on receipt:
   - If request contains client_seq: consult per-customer small in-memory dedupe cache (LRU window keyed by client_epoch + client_seq). If seen -> short-circuit: return cached response without charging. If not seen -> write provisional ledger entry (status=provisional), store a dedupe marker with TTL (default 5m), and forward to serving runtime for execution.
   - If request does not contain client_seq: apply probabilistic admission: compute stable-hash(client_request_fingerprint) and consult a low-FP Bloom filter overlay per-customer for very short window (30s); this reduces duplicates for stateless clients without requiring SDK updates.
3) Post-execution commit path:
   - Successful responses trigger an async commit to change the provisional ledger entry to final (status=committed) and emit a billable event. The commit is idempotent using the provisional idempotency key.
   - If execution fails or times out and client retries with same client_seq, ingest node will reuse provisional entry (no new provisional entry and not double-charge).
4) Reconciliation and expiry:
   - Provisional entries older than X (default 24h) that have no commit get flagged for reconciliation. Reconciliation attempts to match eventual commits or expire provisional entries and either cancel the provisional charge or finalize after manual review depending on policy.

Storage and retention:
- Dedupe markers: in-memory cache per-ingest process + replicated short-term backing store (Redis) with 5m TTL for common cases and a sliding backoff for heavy customers.
- Provisional ledger: append-only store (existing ledger DB/partition) with compacted status. Retain full provisional metadata for 90 days for reconciliation/finance.

Quotas and rate-limits interaction:
- Quota checks are performed at ingest time. For requests that match a dedupe marker, quota is not re-evaluated. For probabilistic stateless path, quota is checked before provisional write. Rate-limit tokens are consumed only once on commit where possible; for low-latency SLOs we may pre-reserve quota on provisional write with quick rollback on dedupe detection.

Edge cases and interoperability:
- Clock skew and client_seq resets: client_epoch used to detect epoch rollover; when epoch changes, server treats new epoch as separate namespace and keeps dedupe markers per-epoch. SDKs encouraged to persist epoch across restarts.
- Multi-region clients: ingest nodes accept client_seq from any region; dedupe cache replicates markers via a lightweight pubsub to avoid cross-region duplicate billing within the dedupe TTL.
acceptance_criteria:
- No duplicate billable events emitted for in-window duplicate requests with client_seq present in 95th percentile synthetic tests.
- Shadow run for 2 weeks on 20% traffic shows duplicate-billing rate reduced by >= 90% relative to baseline.
- Reconciliation workflow surfaces anomalies (>0.01% of provisional entries) with operational runbook.
- No customer reports of lost charges during rollout (finance sign-off).
- Performance overhead at ingest median latency + p95 increase < 8ms across controlled benchmarks.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for provisional ledger state transitions and idempotent commit primitives.
- Integration tests: multi-process SDK emulation with sequence and epoch churn, ensure dedupe semantics.
- Chaos tests: simulate Redis partition, ingest node restarts, and network duplication to validate eventual reconciliation.
- Load test: run 500k RPS synthetic load with 20% retries to measure dedupe cache hit-rate and latency impact.
- Shadow production: accept but do not emit final bill events for a subset (20%) of customers; compare shadow vs baseline billing totals and duplicate rates.
- Regression tests: ensure legacy clients without client_seq are billed exactly as today (unless probabilistic dedupe path triggers prevention).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature gated rollout: start in shadow (accept+defer final billing) on 20% traffic for 2 weeks.
2) Expand to 50% with reconciliation thresholds configured and finance sign-off.
3) Opt-in SDK migration campaign: promote SDK helpers and telemetry to customers for stronger guarantees.
4) Full enable for new customers and opt-in for existing over 6 weeks; continue reconciliation for the rest.
5) Post-rollout: enable short-term dedupe-filter for stateless clients globally.

Fallbacks:
- If Redis dedupe store becomes unhealthy, revert to probabilistic dedupe only and emit alerts; do not change downstream billing semantics.
migration_steps:
- DB: create provisional_ledger table/partition with indexes for customer_id + provisional_id.
- Infra: provision Redis cluster and topic for dedupe marker replication.
- SDK: ship helper that emits client_seq and client_epoch; provide migration doc and examples.
- Backfill: no backfill required. Existing customers without client_seq continue to be charged under current behavior; flag high-retry customers for outreach.
- Feature flag controls: config per-customer to opt-in/opt-out during rollout.
monitoring_and_alerts:
Metrics to add:
- billing.duplicates.provisional_rate (per-customer, per-minute)
- billing.duplicates.committed_after_duplicate (count)
- billing.provisional.count_by_age
- ledger.commit_latency_p50/p95
- reconciliation.aging_provisionals

Alerts:
- alert if provisional > 1% of total billable events for any customer over 1h.
- alert on reconciliation backlog > 10k entries for > 30m.
- alert on dedupe-store Redis error-rate > 0.5% over 5m.

Dashboards:
- per-customer provisional lifecycle timeline, duplicate suppression heatmap, and reconciliation queue depth.

2026-02-24 - Security (Ravi Shah): Reviewed attack surface for dedupe cache poisoning. Recommended signed client_seq tokens for high-risk customers (opt-in).

2026-03-05 - QA (Elena Morales): Ran integration tests with SDK emulator; observed a rare race when epoch rolls over during in-flight request. Filed a small follow-up patch to reject client_seq with last_seen > client_seq+wrap_threshold.

2026-03-08 - Marcus Liu: Load test results uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/duplicate-suppression-load-test showing 92% duplicate reduction at 200k RPS with 20% retries. Two incidents of Redis replication lag observed under 95th percentile load.
2026-03-10 - Finance (Omar Reed): Initial reconciliation sample looks good; provisional->commit ratios align with expectations. Finance requests a weekly report for first month post-rollout.
